scope: Default 128 MiB Market HTTP/parser boundary and event-driven owned stream handoff
problem: The one-slot synchronous reader bridge slept 10 ms whenever its mailbox was empty. At 64 KiB per HTTP chunk this imposed enough latency for a local 128 MiB response to exceed the unchanged 15-second fetch timeout. Original Source accepted the exact limit; initial x64/x86 outcomes matched each other but timed out.
implementation: The producer wakes the event loop when data or terminal settlement arrives. The one-slot mailbox and per-chunk demand semaphore preserve backpressure; arbitrary cancel_check callbacks retain a bounded idle check.
Owned-reader cancellation wakes the producer, shields settlement through repeated cancellation, and joins the completed reader thread before returning.
The qualifier streams synthetic padding directly from a localhost HTTP server and tests actual parser workers; no 128 MiB fixture file or archive is written.

paired.scope: Exact 134217728-byte JSON including padding admitted; declared 134217729 bytes, unlengthened streamed overflow and decoded gzip overflow rejected with original Remote code/message/details. Original fetchIndex/readBody/parser and actual x64/x86 Python transport/worker paths.

native.scope: Demand backpressure, 2048 rapid chunks under operation budget, idle/repeated cancellation, HTTP/LLM/image/account/Market/detail/Fetch/file/MCP direct consumers

failed.scope: Original Source four outcomes succeeded; x86 and x64 were equal before the expected-success assertion failed. x64 raw file was added for subsequent runs; first-run x64 timeout identity is inferred from the successful equality assertion.

cleanup.removed: Owned targeted synthetic workspaces/home/tmp; large data was streamed in memory and all producer/consumer/worker processes exited
cleanup.retained: Failed/successful compact paired observations, inputs, source/native stderr, commands/hash reports and native XML/logs; no large boundary payload remains.

limitations: The upper-bound fixture has an empty plugin array and whitespace padding. This verifies byte transport/UTF-8/parser admission, not arbitrary 128 MiB search-index density or throughput.
The successful boundary run precedes only removal of an unused internal thread flag; final direct-consumer regression covers the final bridge.
No full release gate or actual Win7 OS acceptance is claimed.
